title: Brick Schema
description: Uniform metadata schema for buildings: a vocabulary for describing the points (sensors, setpoints, commands, statuses, alarms), equipment (AHUs, chillers, pumps, VAVs, network devices, etc.), and their relationships (hasPoint/isPointOf, hasPart/isPartOf, feeds/isFedBy, hasUnit via QUDT) in building automation and IoT deployments. Widely used in the building controls / smart buildings community.
publisher: Brick Consortium (UC Berkeley, with industry and academic contributors); ontology hosted at ontology.brickschema.org

models.name: CO2_Level_Sensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - CO2_Level_Sensor
models.description: Measures the concentration of CO2 in air (brick:CO2_Level_Sensor's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology). A dedicated schema for this specific Brick Point leaf class (brick:CO2_Level_Sensor, hierarchy: CO2_Sensor -> Sensor -> Point), alongside the generic Point entity this candidate also publishes. hasQuantity and hasSubstance are fixed (const) here because they are definitional for this exact class, not a per-instance choice.

models.name: Collection
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - Collection
models.description: A logical grouping of points, equipment or other entities that doesn't correspond to a physical or system relationship (brick:Collection and its subclasses, e.g. Automation_Collection). INCOMPLETE BY DESIGN: Collection has no Brick-native membership property in any real Brick example checked (examples/collection/collection.ttl, examples/chiller-system/chiller-plant.ttl, examples/iaq_sensor_deployment) -- every real Collection instance found expresses its membership via RealEstateCore's rec:includes / rec:hasMember, not a Brick property. One of Brick's own example files even comments on this directly. This schema is therefore published as a placeholder (identity + brickClass only, no members) rather than either inventing a non-Brick property or silently omitting Collection altogether. A membership Relationship should be added once the planned RealEstateCore candidate exists for it to point to.

models.name: Equipment
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - Equipment
models.description: A physical piece of equipment in a building's mechanical, electrical or IT systems: an air handling unit, chiller, pump, VAV box, thermostat, network device, etc. (brick:Equipment and its subclasses, Brick Schema). Modeled generically -- see the brickClass property -- rather than as hundreds of separate entity types.

models.name: Occupancy_Sensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - Occupancy_Sensor
models.description: Detects the presence or count of occupants. Unlike the other five classes in this batch, Occupancy_Sensor has no brick:hasSubstance in the source ontology (occupancy isn't a property of a substance/medium the way temperature or a gas concentration is) -- this schema therefore has no hasSubstance property at all, rather than an empty or null one. A dedicated schema for this specific Brick Point leaf class (brick:Occupancy_Sensor, hierarchy: Sensor -> Point), alongside the generic Point entity this candidate also publishes. hasQuantity are fixed (const) here because they are definitional for this exact class, not a per-instance choice.

models.name: PM10_Sensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - PM10_Sensor
models.description: Measures the concentration of PM10 (particulate matter, <=10 micrometers) in air. A dedicated schema for this specific Brick Point leaf class (brick:PM10_Sensor, hierarchy: Particulate_Matter_Sensor -> Sensor -> Point), alongside the generic Point entity this candidate also publishes. hasQuantity and hasSubstance are fixed (const) here because they are definitional for this exact class, not a per-instance choice.

models.name: PM2.5_Sensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - PM2.5_Sensor
models.description: Measures the concentration of PM2.5 (fine particulate matter, <=2.5 micrometers) in air. models.name: Point
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - Point
models.description: A telemetry point exposed by a piece of building Equipment or associated with a Location: a sensor, setpoint, command, status, alarm or parameter (brick:Point and its subclasses, Brick Schema). This candidate models Point generically -- see the brickClass property -- rather than as hundreds of separate entity types.

models.name: Relative_Humidity_Sensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - Relative_Humidity_Sensor
models.description: Measures the relative humidity of air. A dedicated schema for this specific Brick Point leaf class (brick:Relative_Humidity_Sensor, hierarchy: Humidity_Sensor -> Sensor -> Point), alongside the generic Point entity this candidate also publishes. hasQuantity and hasSubstance are fixed (const) here because they are definitional for this exact class, not a per-instance choice.

models.name: System
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - System
models.description: A functional grouping of equipment that together provide a building service, e.g. an HVAC system or a chilled water system (brick:System and its subclasses). INCOMPLETE BY DESIGN: System has no Brick-native membership property in any real Brick example checked (examples/collection/collection.ttl, examples/chiller-system/chiller-plant.ttl, examples/iaq_sensor_deployment) -- every real System instance found expresses its membership via RealEstateCore's rec:includes / rec:hasMember, not a Brick property. This schema is therefore published as a placeholder (identity + brickClass only, no members) rather than either inventing a non-Brick property or silently omitting System altogether. models.name: Zone_Air_Temperature_Sensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - Brick Schema - Zone_Air_Temperature_Sensor
models.description: A temperature sensor for the air within an HVAC zone -- one specific member of Brick's broader Temperature_Sensor family (which also includes e.g. Outside_Air_Temperature_Sensor, Discharge_Air_Temperature_Sensor). Modeled as its own class here because this is the exact leaf class in the real example data (a thermostat's zone sensor); the other family members share the same property shape and could be added the same way. A dedicated schema for this specific Brick Point leaf class (brick:Zone_Air_Temperature_Sensor, hierarchy: Air_Temperature_Sensor -> Temperature_Sensor -> Sensor -> Point), alongside the generic Point entity this candidate also publishes. hasQuantity and hasSubstance are fixed (const) here because they are definitional for this exact class, not a per-instance choice.

title: EDINT Infrastructure Ontology (Ontología de Infraestructura)
description: Vocabulary for representing a municipality's public and private infrastructure facilities (educational, cultural, social, sports and health centers, on-street and off-street parking, shared-bicycle stations) together with the sensors, observations, violations, management roles and organizations involved in operating and monitoring them. Reuses SOSA/SSN (sensors and observations), GeoSPARQL (geometry), schema.org and Dublin Core.
publisher: EDINT - Espacio de Datos para las Infraestructuras Urbanas Inteligentes (EU-funded), with Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM) as technical developer

models.name: AccessObservation
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - AccessObservation
models.description: Observation carried out at any entrance to a municipal facility. This includes pedestrian or vehicle access (edintinf:AccessObservation, subclass of sosa:Observation).

models.name: AccessSensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - AccessSensor
models.description: A device that records the access of people or vehicles. This could be an LPR (license plate recognition) camera, a building entrance door sensor, or other similar devices (edintinf:AccessSensor, subclass of sosa:Sensor).

models.name: BikeSharingStation
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - BikeSharingStation

models.name: CountingObservation

models.name: CountingSensor
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - CountingSensor
models.description: A device that records the number of people or vehicles that it observes (edintinf:CountingSensor, subclass of sosa:Sensor).

models.name: Facility
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - Facility
models.description: It refers to service buildings (public or private), leisure areas, commercial areas or any other element that directly affects mobility, acting as a focus of attraction for persons or vehicles. Source: EDINT Infrastructure Ontology (edintinf:Facility).

models.name: ManagementRole
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - ManagementRole
models.description: The role that the municipal administration or one of its departments plays in the management of a municipal facility. This may include ownership, maintenance, security, among others (edintinf:ManagementRole).

models.name: ObservationPoint
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - ObservationPoint
models.description: Points where access or counting observations can be made using sensors (edintinf:ObservationPoint). The source ontology defines no attributes of its own beyond location; it is the target of the Facility.hasObservationPoint relationship.

models.name: Organization

models.description: Any public or private organization that owns or manages an element of the infrastructure (edintinf:Organization). NOTE: check for overlap with the existing official Smart Data Models 'dataModel.Organization' subject before promoting this candidate.

models.name: Parking

models.description: A Facility specialization for on-street and off-street parking areas. The source ontology (edintinf:Parking) defines no attributes beyond those inherited from Facility; it is distinguished only by its NGSI-LD type and, typically, its infrastructureType value. NOTE: this concept is likely to overlap with the already-existing official Smart Data Models 'dataModel.Parking' subject (e.g. OffStreetParking/OnStreetParking) — check for duplication before promoting this candidate.

models.name: Violation
models.title: Smart Data Models - EDINT Infrastructure - Violation
models.description: Non-compliance or violation of traffic or access rules, road laws or local ordinances by a person or a driver or owner of a vehicle (edintinf:Violation).

title: ERA ERADIS (documents/certification register)
description: ERADIS is one of four registers (alongside RINF, ERATV, EVR) published under the single ERA Ontology v3.3.3 -- see era-rinf's standard-metadata.yaml for the shared ontology-wide context. ERADIS covers the certification and compliance-documentation side of the railway authorisation processes: Certificates (safety certificates for railway undertakings), Conformity Assessment Body (CAB) evidence, assessment/audit checks and restrictions, Certification Level Documents, EC Declarations of Verification/Conformity, document sets, validity constraints on certificates/decisions, and references to the Technical Specifications for Interoperability (TSIs) those checks are performed against.

models.name: CABAuditCheck

The class can be used NoBo, DeBo and/or AsBo checks. Inherits attributes from era:Compliance (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: CABCertificate

Inherits attributes from era:EvidenceDocument (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: CABEvidence

Inherits attributes from era:DocumentSet/era:Evidence (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: CABRestriction
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERADIS - CABRestriction

models.name: Certificate

models.name: ECDeclaration

models.name: ForbiddenAssessmentConstraint
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERADIS - ForbiddenAssessmentConstraint
models.description: Forbidden assessment constraint (era:ForbiddenAssessmentConstraint's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A validity constraint signalling that the combination of CLD type and assessment module is structurally not permitted under this TSI.

models.name: MaxDurationConstraint

models.name: TechnicalSpecForInteroperability

models.name: UnlimitedValidityConstraint

title: ERA ERATV (European Register of Authorised Vehicle Types)
description: ERATV is one of four registers (alongside RINF, ERADIS, EVR) published under the single ERA Ontology v3.3.3 -- see the era-rinf candidate's standard-metadata.yaml for the shared ontology-wide context. ERATV itself covers authorised railway VEHICLE TYPES (as opposed to EVR, which registers individual vehicles): the vehicle type's technical characteristics (dimensions, mass, braking performance, gauging, ETCS/GSM-R/ATO on-board equipment, noise, energy supply compatibility, ...), its per-configuration variants (VehicleTypeConfiguration / VehicleTypeConfigParameterSet, since a single type can be authorised in several technical configurations, e.g. different energy supply systems or ETCS on-board versions), and the type-authorisation process itself (VehicleTypeAuthorisation, its Application, Case, compliance Check, and Restriction).

models.name: VehicleType
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERATV - VehicleType
models.description:
Vehicle Type (era:VehicleType's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A vehicle type that has been authorized to operate on the EU railway infrastructure. Type means a vehicle type defining the basic design characteristics of the vehicle as covered by a type or design examination certificate described in the relevant verification module.

Basic design characteristics means the parameters that are used to identify the vehicle type as specified in the issued vehicle type authorisation and recorded in the European Register of Authorised Vehicle Types ('ERATV').

The above mentioned certificate should be documented using era:certificate.

models.name: VehicleTypeAuthorisation
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERATV - VehicleTypeAuthorisation
models.description:
Vehicle Type Authorisation (era:VehicleTypeAuthorisation's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): (16) the decision issued by the authorising entity based on reasonable assurance that the applicant and the entities involved in the design,
manufacture, verification and validation of the vehicle type have fulfilled their obligations and responsibilities in order to ensure conformity with the essential
requirements of the applicable legislation enabling that a vehicle manufactured according to this design may be placed on the market and may be used safely in the
area of use of the vehicle type according to the conditions for use of the vehicle and other restrictions, when applicable, specified in the vehicle type authorisation
and to be applied to all vehicle authorised in conformity to this type; Inherits attributes from era:Permission (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: VehicleTypeAuthorisationApplication
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERATV - VehicleTypeAuthorisationApplication
models.description:
Vehicle Type Authorisation Case (era:VehicleTypeAuthorisationApplication's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): The request, as submitted by the Applicant in line with (EU)2018/545, to allow the vehicle type authorisation and/or the vehicle authorisation for placing on the market.
The application consists of one or more authorisation cases as described in Art. 14 of (EU)2018/545, and for authorisations before the Fourth Railway Package, a HistoricalAuthorisationCase must be used.

The outcome of the application process is a `era:VehicleAuthorisation` or `era:VehicleTypeAuthorisation`. Inherits attributes from era:Request (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: VehicleTypeAuthorisationCase
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERATV - VehicleTypeAuthorisationCase
models.description:
Vehicle Type Authorisation Case (era:VehicleTypeAuthorisationCase's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): The process, as selected by the Applicant in line with (EU)2018/545, allowing the vehicle type authorisation and/or the vehicle authorisation for placing on the market.
The type of authorisation cases are described in Art. 14 of (EU)2018/545, and for authorisations before the Fourth Railway Package, a HistoricalAuthorisationCase must be used.

Each authorisation case supports a VehicleTypeAuthorisationApplication and is determined by exactly one VehicleType, and a set of Vehicles, which can be empty in some cases.

For authorisations before the (EU)2018/545 legislation, use `era:VehicleAuthorisationCase. Inherits attributes from era:Case (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: VehicleTypeAuthorisationCheck
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERATV - VehicleTypeAuthorisationCheck
models.description:
Vehicle Type Authorisation Compliance Check (era:VehicleTypeAuthorisationCheck's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A verification result as executed by a competent body on a section of a legal reference. The check can be positive or negative, and in the latter case, a restriction is expected.

This Class is used to improve the link between verification outcomes and the verified scope of that process, and support its structured documentation. Inherits attributes from era:Compliance (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: VehicleTypeAuthorisationRestriction
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERATV - VehicleTypeAuthorisationRestriction
models.description:
Vehicle Type Authorisation Restriction (era:VehicleTypeAuthorisationRestriction's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): Restrictions, like coded and non-coded conditions for use, to be taken into account in the context of a Vehicle (Type) Authorisation.

The restrictions are recorded by the Authorising Entities, possibly deduced during underlying verification and certification processes by competent bodies, and if possible are documented with a link
to the legal reference and sections therein.

In most cases, the Restriction will be dependent of a VehicleTypeConfiguration. Inherits attributes from era:Restriction (inlined here rather than via schema $ref, per this repo's convention).

models.name: VehicleTypeConfigParameterSet
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERATV - VehicleTypeConfigParameterSet
models.description: Vehicle type configuration parameter set (era:VehicleTypeConfigParameterSet's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): Stub class linking a VehicleTypeConfiguration (`era:forConfiguration`) with parameters of the VehicleType that depend on that configuration.

models.name: VehicleTypeConfiguration
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA ERATV - VehicleTypeConfiguration
models.description: Vehicle type configuration (era:VehicleTypeConfiguration's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): The combination of supported Gauge, Energy Systems and/or CCO Systems for a vehicle type

title: ERA EVR (European Vehicle Register)
description: EVR is the last of the four registers (alongside RINF, ERATV, ERADIS) published under the single ERA Ontology v3.3.3 -- see era-rinf's standard-metadata.yaml for the shared ontology-wide context. EVR registers individual VEHICLES (as opposed to ERATV, which authorises vehicle TYPES): each vehicle's identity and technical data as manufactured (European Vehicle Number, keeper, owner, ECM, manufacturing details), its Vehicle Keeper Marking (VKM), national-level registration properties defined by individual member states, and the registration process itself (VehicleRegistration, its Application, Case, compliance Check, and Restriction) plus the closely related vehicle (not vehicle-type) authorisation-for-placing-in-service process (VehicleAuthorisation, Case, Notification).

models.name: ERTMSErrorChangeRequest
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA EVR - ERTMSErrorChangeRequest
models.description: ERTMS error change request (era:ERTMSErrorChangeRequest's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): SKOS concept representing a change request (CR) classified as an error in the ERTMS specifications and analysed by the Agency to identify whether it may prevent the system from providing normal service under Article 10 of the CCS TSI.

models.name: NationalRegistrationProperty
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA EVR - NationalRegistrationProperty
models.description: National Registration Property (era:NationalRegistrationProperty's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A property defined at national level by a member state for vehicle registration purposes. Each member state may define its own set of such properties, identified by a national property identifier string. This class avoids creating individual era: predicates for each member-state-specific registration field. The member state is determined by the registeringMemberState of the parent VehicleRegistrationCase.

models.name: Vehicle
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA EVR - Vehicle
models.description: Vehicle (era:Vehicle's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): A specific vehicle or wagon able and allowed to operate over railway infrastructure.

models.name: VehicleAuthorisation
models.title: Smart Data Models - ERA EVR - VehicleAuthorisation
models.description:
Vehicle Authorisation for Placing on the Market (era:VehicleAuthorisation's own definition, verbatim, in the source ontology): (15) the decision issued by the authorising entity based on a reasonable assurance that the applicant and the entities involved in the design,

title: ERA RINF (Register of Infrastructure)
description: RINF is one of four registers (alongside ERATV, ERADIS, EVR) published under the single ERA Ontology v3.3.3. RINF itself covers the physical and topological railway infrastructure of the EU network: operational points, tracks (running tracks and sidings), sections of line, tunnels, bridges, platforms, level crossings, switches, signals, electrification (contact line systems, pantograph/phase-separation parameters), control-command and signalling (ETCS, Radio Block Centres, train detection systems, GSM-R), and the abstract network/topology graph model (NetElement, LinearElement, NetRelation, linear positioning systems) that ties physical assets to a navigable network representation. This candidate is the RINF sub-standard only; ERATV (authorised vehicle types), ERADIS (authorisation/certification documents), and EVR (vehicle register) are separate sub-standards of the same ontology, planned as later candidates under their own standards/ folders (era-eratv, era-eradis, era-evr) since they are distinct subject areas with their own entity graphs, sharing only a handful of admin classes (era:Body, era:OrganisationRole) with RINF.

title: Gaia-X Ontology (Trust Framework / Self-Description Schema)
description: The Gaia-X ontology defines the vocabulary used to write Self-Descriptions (verifiable-credential-based claims) for participants, resources and service offerings in a Gaia-X data space / federated cloud ecosystem. It spans infrastructure and service-offering classes (compute, storage, network, container/function-as-a-service, data products), physical and virtual resource classes (CPU, GPU, Memory, Disk, Datacenter, Device, ServerFlavor), connectivity and QoS metrics (Latency, Jitter, PacketLoss, Throughput, BandWidth, RoundTripTime), and a large body of governance, legal, compliance, security-policy and credential/trust-anchor classes (LegalPerson, TermsAndConditions, DataUsageAgreement, InformationSecurity Policies, LabelCredential, EvidenceTemplate, ...) that describe how a participant or resource is governed and certified rather than what it physically measures. This candidate translates the full v2111 class list (165 classes) into one candidate per class under models/.
